title: Enterprise Distributed DAG Saga Orchestrator with Cycle Detection, Retries, and Reverse Compensation
objective: Implement a resilient, enterprise-grade Distributed DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) Saga Orchestration Engine in Python/FastAPI using SQLite and AsyncIO. The engine must support multi-tenant distributed transaction workflows defined as arbitrary dependency DAGs, Kahn's algorithm cycle detection, concurrent topological forward dispatching, configurable retry policies with exponential backoff and step timeouts, Idempotency-Key request deduplication, multi-phase saga lifecycle state machines (pending, running, completed, compensating, compensated, compensation_failed), in-flight saga pause/resume controls, and parallel reverse topological compensation with an append-only SQLite state transition journal.
motivation: Distributed microservice architectures require fault-tolerant transactional guarantees without two-phase locking. Implementing an enterprise DAG Saga coordinator from scratch tests asynchronous concurrency primitives, graph algorithms (topological sorting, cycle detection), resilient network dispatch with backoff, and distributed state machine persistence.
difficultyExplanation:
1. Topological Graph Validation & Kahn's Cycle Detection: Efficiently validating dynamic JSON DAGs, rejecting cycles and dangling dependency references with structured RFC-style error responses before committing transaction state to SQLite.
2. Concurrent Forward Scheduling with Exponential Retries & Timeouts: Dispatching independent frontier nodes in parallel while orchestrating non-blocking async HTTP timeouts and retry backoff intervals without blocking other concurrent saga executions.
3. Reverse Topological Parallel Compensation & Journal Audit: Correctly resolving the exact reverse topological dependency graph of completed steps to execute compensation HTTP endpoints concurrently across independent branches and recording immutable audit journal entries for every state transition.
environmentSummary: Python 3.11-slim container with FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pytest, HTTPX, SQLite3, and pre-configured Pydantic models in /app.
oracleStrategy: Reference implementation in solution/ providing an SQLite-backed async worker engine with Kahn's cycle detection, topological DAG scheduler, HTTP retry/timeout dispatcher, reverse leaf compensator, and REST journal endpoints.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh which executes multi-stage hidden pytest suites covering:
1. DAG Cycle Detection & Dangling Dependency Validation (Kahn's algorithm rejection).
2. Concurrent Forward Topological Execution across Parallel Diamond & Wide DAGs.
3. Transient 5xx Retry Backoff & Step Timeout Handling.
4. Reverse Topological Compensation Cascades upon Unrecoverable Failures.
5. In-flight Saga Pause/Resume Controls & SQLite Audit Journal Integrity.
binarySuccessCondition: Passes 100% of all hidden test suites across all 5 verification phases with full reward score >= 0.95.
partialScoreStrategy:
Monotone scoring breakdown:
- 20%: DAG cycle detection & invalid dependency validation.
- 20%: Forward parallel topological execution on diamond DAGs.
- 20%: Step retries with exponential backoff and timeout handling.
- 20%: Reverse topological parallel compensation rollbacks.
- 20%: In-flight pause/resume controls and append-only state journal audit.
anticipatedExploits:
1. Sequential single-threaded step execution: Verifier measures execution wall-clock time across parallel branches to enforce concurrent HTTP dispatching.
2. In-memory volatile state: Verifier queries SQLite database tables and journal entries directly across separate client connections.
